paragraphs: Hyman cites Bereshit Rabbah 13:15 and proposes that the name should read Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi.

notes.text: The initials ל״ם remain unresolved. Hyman’s proposed Yehoshua ben Levi reading is retained as an attributed correction.

The earlier local English invented a commentator “L-M”; that attribution is withdrawn. The source has unresolved ובל״ם before צ״ל, “it should read,” introducing the proposed Yehoshua ben Levi reading. A conjecture ובל״ס would mean “and without doubt,” giving Hyman’s proposal confident force if that reading were established; it is not adopted as a verified letter correction. No new Bereshit Rabbah nonmatch or external commentator is claimed.

Theodor’s Bereshit Rabbah, chapter 13, section 15 (pp. 124–125), names Rabbi Yochanan bar Levi in the discussion of the benefits of rain. The apparatus records ben Levi as a variant. The same passage is numbered 13:16 in the Torat Emet digital edition. Hyman’s own correction to Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi is preceded by the printed ובל״ם, which may represent his usual ובל״ס (“and without doubt”).
